t: Sikhism began with Guru Nanak’s teaching in the Punjab around 1500: one God, remembered in prayer, served through honest work and sharing, and found by all people equally, whatever their caste.
Nine Gurus after him built its institutions: the Golden Temple at Amritsar, the scripture of the Guru Granth Sahib and, under Guru Gobind Singh in 1699, the Khalsa order of initiated Sikhs.
Persecuted under the later Mughals, Sikhs built their own empire under Ranjit Singh, and today some 25 to 30 million Sikhs live in the Punjab and across the world.
dyk: The free kitchen (langar) of the Golden Temple at Amritsar serves meals to tens of thousands of people every day, of any faith or none, all of them seated together on the floor as equals.
ev: Guru Nanak’s spiritual experience at the river Bein near Sultanpur Lodhi begins his mission
Guru Ram Das founds the city of Amritsar around its sacred pool
Guru Arjan installs the Adi Granth, the Sikh scripture, in the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar
Guru Arjan is executed under the Mughal emperor Jahangir
Guru Tegh Bahadur is executed in Delhi on the orders of Aurangzeb
Guru Gobind Singh founds the Khalsa at Anandpur on the festival of Vaisakhi
Ranjit Singh takes Lahore and goes on to found the Sikh Empire
The Indian army’s Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple, followed by the assassination of Indira Gandhi and anti-Sikh violence

f.founder: Guru Nanak (1469–1539), followed by nine Gurus to Guru Gobind Singh (d. 1708)
f.scriptures: The Guru Granth Sahib, compiled by Guru Arjan in 1604 and completed under Guru Gobind Singh
f.followers: About 25 to 30 million, most of them in the Punjab, with large communities in Britain, Canada and the United States
